title: Left-shift scan output
statement: Let $B$ and $\Gamma$ be sets, let $\operatorname{get}:\Gamma\to B$ and $\operatorname{set}:\Gamma\to B\to\Gamma$, let $b_0\in B$, and let $w$ be a finite word over $\Gamma$. A two-pass scan first leaves the state and symbols unchanged from left to right, then scans from right to left, replacing each symbol $\gamma$ by $\operatorname{set}(\gamma,b)$ and updating the state to $\operatorname{get}(\gamma)$. The final state is the first value of $\operatorname{get}$ along $w$, or $b_0$ if $w$ is empty; the output replaces each symbol of $w$ by setting its stored value to the value of $\operatorname{get}$ at the next symbol, using $b_0$ for the last symbol.
